 Wildcats to Visit Pitt on Tuesday Night
 Former BIG EAST rivals to meet at 7 p.m. at the Petersen Events Center
 Story Links
 VILLANOVA, Pa. – As a former point guard who once transferred to a new college home, Villanova head coach Kevin Willard has an appreciation for the transition junior point guard Elijah Crawford is making after playing last season at UIC.
"This has been a huge adjustment for Elijah because he was asked to score a lot last year," said Willard on Saturday night after the Wildcats' 99-62 victory over Rider at Finneran Pavilion. "For us, at times, he's out there with guys that need to get the basketball.
"I think he's doing a really good job of balancing, 'when do I need to be aggressive to score?' or 'when do I need to find guys?' He's getting a little bit more comfortable. He's working really hard on the defensive end too. He's a naturally great passer in the pick and roll.
"He's just trying to find that balance between when can I look to score, and when do I look to pass. He's doing a good job figuring that out."
The next step in that process comes Tuesday night when the Wildcats (3-1 overall) face former longtime BIG EAST rival Pittsburgh (4-0 overall) at the Petersen Events Center (7 p.m./ACC Network and the Villanova Sports Radio Network). It is a homecoming for Willard, who played the final two seasons of his college career with the Panthers after transferring from Western Kentucky to follow his father, Ralph Willard, who was named Pitt's head coach in 1994.
This will be Vilanova's first visit to play at Pittsburgh since 2013. Following that season the Panthers departed the BIG EAST for the Atlantic Coast Conference. The Wildcats' last victory over Pitt on its home court dates to Feb. 17, 1996 – a 67-64 win at Fitzgerald Field House. The Panthers own a 10-game winning streak at home against Nova.
Of course, the Wildcats did gain an important win in the series on a neutral floor when they knocked off the Panthers 78-76 in the 2009 East Regional Final in Boston. Scottie Reynolds – another point guard – hit the game-winning basket with under a second to play.
The series between the teams is deadlocked at 33. Villanova posted a 79-61 win in last year's clash at Finneran Pavilion.
The Wildcats have won three straight since dropping a 74-72 decision to Notre Dame on Nov. 1 at the Eternal City Tip-Off in Rome. With 10 newcomers to the roster and a handful of key injuries, Willard has been sampling several lineup combinations. On Saturday night, Nova was without 7-3 center Luigi Suigo (right knee soreness) and lost guard Darryl Simmons midway through the first half to a leg injury.
The better health news was that Kwame Evans, Jr. , who missed much of the preseason, logged a season-high 21:21 against Rider and contributed his first VU double-double with 14 points and 10 rebounds.
Crawford has been a steady hand at the wheel of the offense in the early going. The native of Georgia ranks fourth in the BIG EAST with 6.25 assists per game and seventh in the conference in assist-to-turnover ratio (3.13 with 25 assists and eight turnovers).
Jay Alter and Randolph Childress will be the announcers for this game on the ACC Network. Ryan Fannon and Whitey Rigsby will have the call on the Villanova Sports Radio Network (Sirius XM channel 264).
On Monday, Suigo was named BIG EAST Freshman of the Week while Devin Royal was selected to the BIG EAST weekly Honor Roll.
Villanova's big week continues on Saturday night when the Wildcats host 2026 NCAA champion Michigan at Xfinity Mobile Arena at 7 p.m. Tickets remain available and may be purchased at this link Print Friendly Version
